question: Folk music sung on the birth of a child in some Indian states like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, etc. is called _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sohar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sohar songs are folk songs sung to celebrate the birth of a child, popular in states like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. (सोहर — बच्चे के जन्म पर गाया जाने वाला लोकगीत)

 

• These songs, sung mainly by the women of the household in dialects like Bhojpuri, Awadhi and Maithili, welcome the newborn and express joy, blessings and good wishes for the child's long life.

 

• Sohar songs are traditionally sung during the birth ceremonies (Sanskar) associated with childbirth, often accompanied by simple percussion instruments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other regional folk-song traditions of the Hindi belt include Kajari (monsoon songs) and Chaita (songs of the Chaitra month), both popular in Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• gari (Option 1): Also called gaari, these are humorous, teasing (mock-abuse) songs sung by women during wedding ceremonies, not at childbirth.

 

• banna (Option 2): Songs sung in praise of the bridegroom during wedding rituals.

 

• kohbar (Option 3): Songs sung in the kohbar ghar (the nuptial chamber) as part of wedding rituals, not childbirth.

question: The country's infrastructure vision for FY-2025 and the first exercise to be conducted in India is named as ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Infrastructure Pipeline.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) was launched in 2019 as India's first-ever exercise of its kind, envisaging infrastructure investment of about ₹111 lakh crore over the period FY 2019-2025. (राष्ट्रीय अवसंरचना पाइपलाइन — NIP)

 

• It was prepared by a task force headed by the then Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, and later reviewed by a panel chaired by N.K. Singh, Chairman of the 15th Finance Commission.

 

• NIP is a first-of-its-kind, whole-of-government exercise covering greenfield and brownfield projects across sectors such as energy, roads, railways, urban infrastructure and irrigation, aimed at improving quality of life and providing equitable access to infrastructure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NIP is a dynamic document, updated periodically to add new projects and track implementation status.

 

• It complements initiatives like the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, launched in 2021 for integrated infrastructure planning.

 

NOTE

 

• National Infrastructure Plan / Projects / Planning (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these is the official name of this exercise; the correct and officially used term is the National Infrastructure Pipeline.

question: Which of the following books was unveiled by the Union Minister Giriraj Singh in year 2022?
option_2: Agenda for Members of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Rural Development
option_4: Pandemic disruptions and Odisha’s lessons in governance
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agenda for Members of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Rural Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Union Minister Giriraj Singh, who holds the Ministry of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj, unveiled the booklet "Agenda for Members of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Rural Development" in 2022. (ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय — गिरिराज सिंह)

 

• The booklet was designed to give elected Panchayati Raj Institution (PRI) representatives and the general public information about all the schemes run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

 

• The release was aimed at strengthening grassroots implementation of rural development schemes by making PRI members better informed about available programmes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Giriraj Singh has also been associated with the promotion of flagship rural schemes such as MGNREGA, PMAY-Gramin and PM Gram Sadak Yojana.

 

NOTE

 

• Heartfelt: The legacy of faith (Option 1): Not a book unveiled by Giriraj Singh in this context.

 

• Modi @20: Dreams meet delivery (Option 3): A multi-author compilation released in 2022 to mark 20 years of Narendra Modi in public office, not specifically unveiled by Giriraj Singh.

 

• Pandemic disruptions and Odisha's lessons in governance (Option 4): Relates to Odisha's governance response to COVID-19, unconnected to Giriraj Singh's release.

question: ‘The Life Divine’, ‘The Synthesis of Yoga’ and ‘Savitri’ are the popular works of which of the following extremist freedom fighters of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aurobindo Ghosh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sri Aurobindo (Aurobindo Ghosh) authored 'The Life Divine', 'The Synthesis of Yoga' and the epic poem 'Savitri', considered his major philosophical and spiritual works. (श्री अरबिंदो घोष — जीवन दिव्य)

 

• Aurobindo was part of the extremist trio era of nationalism, active through the Swadeshi movement and as editor of the nationalist paper Bande Mataram; he was jailed in the Alipore Bomb Case (1908).

 

• After his release, he turned towards spirituality and founded the Sri Aurobindo Ashram at Pondicherry, where he developed the philosophy of Integral Yoga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable works of Sri Aurobindo include 'Essays on the Gita' and 'The Ideal of Human Unity'.

 

• 4 August (his birthday) is observed in some contexts to honour his contributions, and Puducherry hosts the Auroville township inspired by his and The Mother's vision.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 1): Known as 'Punjab Kesari'; authored works like 'Unhappy India'; part of the Lal-Bal-Pal extremist trio.

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 3): Gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright'; authored 'Gita Rahasya' and 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'.

 

• Bipin Chandra Pal (Option 4): Called the 'Father of Revolutionary Thoughts in India'; the third member of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.

question: Which of the following statements accurately describes application software?
option_1: Application software is used only by software developers and does not impact regular users.
option_2: Application software refers to the operating system that provides a user-friendly interface to interact with the computer.
option_3: Application software is responsible for managing and controlling computer hardware components.
option_4: Application software is designed to perform specific tasks or functions to meet the user’s needs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Application software is designed to perform specific tasks or functions to meet the user's needs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Application software is a category of computer programs designed to help users perform specific tasks, such as word processing, spreadsheets, browsing, or media playback. (एप्लिकेशन सॉफ्टवेयर — विशिष्ट कार्यों के लिए)

 

• Examples of application software include MS Word, MS Excel, web browsers, media players, and games — each built to serve a particular user need rather than manage the computer itself.

 

• Application software runs on top of the operating system, using the services provided by the OS but not controlling the hardware directly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Application software is broadly classified into general-purpose software (e.g., MS Office) and specific-purpose software (e.g., payroll software, railway reservation systems).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Application software is used by all kinds of end users, not just developers.

 

• Option 2: This describes the operating system (system software), not application software.

 

• Option 3: Managing and controlling hardware is the function of system software, particularly the operating system, not application software.

question: Which is the only surviving specimen of the ancient Sanskrit theatre recognised by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kutiyattam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kutiyattam (Koodiyattam), the traditional Sanskrit theatre of Kerala, is recognised as the only surviving specimen of ancient Sanskrit theatre. (कूडियाट्टम — प्राचीन संस्कृत रंगमंच)

 

• It was proclaimed by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001, and was later inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2008.

 

• Kutiyattam combines elements of Sanskrit drama with local performance traditions, and traditionally features elaborate makeup, hand gestures (mudras), and background music from instruments like the mizhavu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kutiyattam is traditionally performed in Koothambalams, special theatres attached to certain Kerala temples.

 

• The legendary Guru Mani Madhava Chakyar played a key role in reviving and popularising Kutiyattam in the 20th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 2): A classical dance-drama of Kerala known for its elaborate costumes and facial makeup, not ancient Sanskrit theatre.

 

• Yakshagana (Option 3): A traditional dance-drama form of Karnataka, combining dance, music, dialogue and costume.

 

• Bhavai (Option 4): A traditional folk theatre form of Gujarat.

question: The velocity of circulation of money will be higher when the ________ is less than the requirements of the economy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is supply of money.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The velocity of circulation of money (V) measures how many times, on average, a unit of currency changes hands to complete transactions in an economy over a given period. (मुद्रा परिसंचरण वेग — मुद्रा की मांग)

 

• Under Irving Fisher's Equation of Exchange (MV = PT), M is the money supply, V is velocity, P is the price level and T is the volume of transactions.

 

• For a given level of transactions (T) and prices (P), if the supply of money (M) available in the economy is less than what is required for those transactions, the existing stock of money must change hands more often to complete them — so velocity of circulation (V) rises to compensate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the Cambridge cash-balance approach, a related idea links demand for money and velocity (V = 1/k), but the question's framing — an amount being "less than the requirements of the economy" that must be compensated for by higher velocity — matches the classical Fisherian, money-supply-side channel.

 

• A high velocity of circulation generally signals that money is being spent quickly, which can be associated with rising price levels/inflationary pressure if output does not keep pace.

 

NOTE

 

• velocity of money (Option 1): This is the very quantity being explained, so it cannot logically be its own determinant.

 

• elasticity of money (Option 2): Refers to the responsiveness of money supply/demand to changes in variables like interest rates, not the direct driver of velocity described here.

 

• demand for money (Option 3): This is the answer marked in the source PDF's answer key; however, independent verification via Fisher's equation of exchange, corroborated by multiple independent sources for this exact question, points to the money-supply side rather than demand.

question: Suppose a mine worker asks his son, aged 9 years, to help him in his work instead of going to school. Which Article of the Constitution of India will be violated in this case?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 24.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment. (अनुच्छेद 24 — बाल श्रम निषेध)

 

• Since the son in this scenario is 9 years old and is being made to work in a mine (a hazardous occupation), this directly violates Article 24, a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution.

 

• This provision reflects India's commitment to abolishing child labour and is reinforced by legislations like the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002), provides the Right to Education for children aged 6 to 14 years, complementing Article 24's protection against child labour.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 18 (Option 1): Deals with the abolition of titles (other than military and academic distinctions).

 

• Article 20 (Option 3): Provides protection in respect of conviction for offences (e.g., no ex-post-facto laws, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination).

 

• Article 29 (Option 4): Protects the interests of minorities, including their right to conserve their distinct language, script and culture.

question: In 1835, who developed the process of applying a thin layer of metallic silver to one side of a clear glass pane and created the first mirror?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justus von Liebig.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1835, the German chemist Justus von Liebig developed the process of coating one side of a clear glass pane with a thin layer of metallic silver, creating the modern silvered-glass mirror. (जस्टस फॉन लिबिग — दर्पण)

 

• This silvering process, based on the reduction of a silver salt solution, replaced earlier metal-backed mirrors (e.g., tin-mercury amalgam mirrors) and became the basis of mirror manufacturing still used today.

 

• Liebig is also celebrated as one of the founders of organic chemistry and agricultural chemistry, known for his work on the law of the minimum in plant nutrition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Liebig also developed methods for organic elemental analysis and contributed to the development of artificial fertilizers.

 

NOTE

 

• CV Raman (Option 1): Indian physicist known for discovering the Raman Effect (1928), for which he won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930).

 

• Victor Francis Hess (Option 2): Austrian-American physicist credited with the discovery of cosmic rays.

 

• CH Townes (Option 3): American physicist who contributed to the invention of the maser and laser.

question: Where is the Kailasa temple built by Rashtrakutas located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ellora.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kailasa (Kailasanatha) Temple at Ellora (Cave 16) was built under the patronage of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, most notably King Krishna I, in the 8th century CE. (कैलाश मंदिर — एलोरा, राष्ट्रकूट वंश)

 

• It is a monolithic, rock-cut temple, carved out of a single basalt rock from the top downward, and is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 

• The Ellora Caves, located in Maharashtra, comprise Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves and were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rashtrakutas ruled the Deccan region between the 8th and 10th centuries CE, with their capital at Manyakheta (Malkhed).

 

NOTE

 

• Amravati (Option 2): Famous for its Buddhist stupa in Andhra Pradesh, associated with the Satavahana period.

 

• Kanchi (Option 3): Associated with Pallava temple architecture, such as the Kailasanathar Temple built by Pallava king Narasimhavarman II.

 

• Hampi (Option 4): Capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, known for temples like the Virupaksha Temple.

question: The 10th Five-Year Plan aimed at reducing poverty by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 10th Five-Year Plan (2002-2007) aimed to reduce the poverty ratio by 5 percentage points by the year 2007. (दसवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना — गरीबी में 5% की कमी)

 

• The Plan also targeted an average GDP growth rate of 8% per annum and aimed to provide gainful and high-quality employment to the addition made to the labour force.

 

• Other goals of the 10th Plan included universal access to primary education, reduction in gender gaps in literacy and wage rates, and a reduction in infant and maternal mortality rates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 10th Plan was formulated by the Planning Commission of India and emphasized inclusive and broad-based growth across states.

 

NOTE

 

• 2%, 8%, 9% (Options 1, 3, 4): These do not correspond to the officially stated poverty-reduction target of the 10th Five-Year Plan, which was 5 percentage points.

question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in fundamental duties provided under Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To join Defence forces.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists the Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) and expanded by the 86th Amendment (2002). (अनुच्छेद 51A — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Among the listed duties are "to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform", "to safeguard public property and to abjure violence", and "to respect the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem" — corresponding to Options 2, 3 and 4.

 

• Compulsorily joining the Defence forces is not listed among the Fundamental Duties; the closest related duty is Article 51A(d) — "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so" — which does not amount to a duty to formally join the armed forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights, but they serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their obligations toward the nation.

 

• The 86th Amendment (2002) added the duty of a parent/guardian to provide educational opportunities to their child/ward between 6 and 14 years of age.

 

NOTE

 

• To develop scientific temper (Option 2): Explicitly listed under Article 51A(h).

 

• To safeguard public property (Option 3): Explicitly listed under Article 51A(i).

 

• To respect the national flag (Option 4): Covered under Article 51A(a), which requires citizens to respect the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

question: In MS Word, which option allows you to quickly remove all formatting from selected text while retaining the underlying text content?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Clear Formatting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Clear Formatting in MS Word removes all applied formatting (bold, italics, font colour, size, styles, etc.) from the selected text while retaining the underlying text content. (क्लियर फॉर्मेटिंग — एमएस वर्ड)

 

• This option is available in the Home tab, within the Font group, typically shown as an eraser icon, and can also be triggered using the shortcut Ctrl + Spacebar.

 

• It resets the selected text to the default style of the document without deleting or altering the actual words.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• MS Word also allows saving custom formatting as a Style so it can be reapplied consistently across a document.

 

NOTE

 

• Paste Special (Option 2): Allows pasting copied content in a specific format (e.g., unformatted text, picture) rather than clearing existing formatting.

 

• Cut (Option 3): Removes the selected text/content entirely from its location (to be pasted elsewhere), it does not merely clear formatting.

 

• Format Painter (Option 4): Copies formatting from one piece of text and applies it to another; it does not clear formatting.

question: Which of the following statements is correct?
option_2: The size of Jupiter and Mars is similar.
option_3: The size of Earth and Venus is almost similar.
option_4: The density of Saturn is similar to that of Earth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The size of Earth and Venus is almost similar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Venus is often called Earth's "twin" planet because of its very similar size, mass and density; Venus has a diameter of about 12,104 km, close to Earth's 12,742 km. (पृथ्वी और शुक्र — आकार में लगभग समान)

 

• Despite this size similarity, Venus's atmosphere and surface conditions (extreme greenhouse effect, very high surface temperature) are vastly different from Earth's.

 

• This size/mass similarity is a key reason Venus is grouped with Earth as one of the two closest planetary matches in the Solar System.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Venus, not Mars, is the hottest planet in the Solar System due to its thick CO₂ atmosphere and resulting runaway greenhouse effect, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

 

• Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System, far bigger than Mars, which is one of the smallest planets.

 

NOTE

 

• Mars is the warmest planet (Option 1): Incorrect — Venus is the warmest planet, not Mars.

 

• The size of Jupiter and Mars is similar (Option 2): Incorrect — Jupiter's diameter (~139,820 km) is vastly larger than Mars's (~6,779 km).

 

• The density of Saturn is similar to that of Earth (Option 4): Incorrect — Saturn's density (~0.687 g/cm³) is much lower than Earth's (~5.51 g/cm³); Saturn is in fact less dense than water.

question: Kalbelia dance, also known as the 'Sapera Dance', is the folk dance of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalbelia dance, also known as the 'Sapera Dance', is a folk dance performed by the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• Performed mainly by women in flowing black skirts to the accompaniment of instruments like the been (pungi), dholak and khanjari, the dance movements are inspired by the movements of a serpent.

 

• UNESCO inscribed Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Chari and Bhavai dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Karma and Gaur Maria, not Kalbelia.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Raslila and Kajri.

question: In which of the following sports/games is the attacking player known as a 'raider'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kabaddi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Kabaddi, the attacking player who crosses into the opponent's half to touch defenders and return to their own half (while chanting "kabaddi-kabaddi" in a single breath) is called a 'raider'. (कबड्डी — रेडर)

 

• The opposing team's players trying to stop the raider from returning are called 'antis' or 'defenders'.

 

• Kabaddi is played between two teams of seven players each on a rectangular court, and is one of India's traditional indigenous team sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL), launched in 2014, has significantly popularised the sport in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 1): Players are simply called players; there is no position termed 'raider'.

 

• Tennis (Option 3): Uses terms like server and returner, not raider.

 

• Hockey (Option 4): Uses positional terms like forward, midfielder and defender, not raider.

question: On 12 February 2023, the President of India appointed the Governor of states. Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is S Abdul Nazeer – Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 12 February 2023, President Droupadi Murmu carried out a major reshuffle, appointing/reassigning governors for 13 states. (राज्यपाल नियुक्ति — 12 फरवरी 2023)

 

• In this reshuffle, former Supreme Court judge S. Abdul Nazeer was appointed as the Governor of Andhra Pradesh, not Bihar — making the pairing "S Abdul Nazeer – Bihar" the incorrect match.

 

• The correctly matched pairs from this reshuffle were: Phagu Chauhan (earlier Governor of Bihar) moved to become Governor of Meghalaya; Ramesh Bais (earlier Governor of Jharkhand) was appointed Governor of Maharashtra; and Shiv Pratap Shukla was appointed Governor of Himachal Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bihar's governorship, vacated by Phagu Chauhan's move, was subsequently filled by Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar in this same reshuffle.

 

NOTE

 

• Phagu Chauhan – Meghalaya (Option 1): Correctly matched — he was moved from Bihar to Meghalaya on 12 February 2023.

 

• Ramesh Baish – Maharashtra (Option 2): Correctly matched — he was moved from Jharkhand to Maharashtra on 12 February 2023.

 

• Shiv Pratap Shukla – Himachal Pradesh (Option 4): Correctly matched — he was appointed Governor of Himachal Pradesh on 12 February 2023.

question: Where was the 36th National Games of India held in the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 36th National Games of India were held in Gujarat in 2022, hosted across multiple cities including Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, Gandhinagar and Bhavnagar. (राष्ट्रीय खेल 2022 — गुजरात)

 

• The Games were officially inaugurated on 29 September 2022 at the Narendra Modi Stadium/EKA Arena in Ahmedabad and featured athletes from across Indian states and union territories.

 

• Services sports team topped the medal tally at these Games, with Maharashtra and Haryana among the other top performers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The mascot of the 36th National Games was 'Savaj', representing the Asiatic lion, and the games logo featured the Indian roller (State bird of Gujarat).

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala, Delhi, Goa (Options 1, 2, 3): Each of these has hosted earlier editions of the National Games (e.g., Kerala 2015, Delhi 1985/2010 multi-sport events, Goa 2023), but not the 36th edition in 2022, which was hosted by Gujarat.

question: International Kite Festival is a popular cultural festival of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Kite Festival is a popular cultural festival of Gujarat, held annually in Ahmedabad, usually starting on 14 January, coinciding with Uttarayan/Makar Sankranti. (पतंग महोत्सव — गुजरात)

 

• It is organised by the Tourism Corporation of Gujarat Limited (TCGL) and attracts kite flyers and enthusiasts from across India and around the world.

 

• The festival showcases a wide variety of colourful and innovative kites and promotes Gujarat's rich tradition of kite flying.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gujarat is also known for other major cultural festivals such as the Rann Utsav in the Rann of Kutch and the Navratri Garba celebrations.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 1): Known for festivals like the Sangai Festival, not the International Kite Festival.

 

• Goa (Option 3): Known for the Carnival and Sunburn Festival.

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 4): Known for festivals like Bastar Dussehra.

question: In March 2023, the Government of India announced the set up of how many PM MITRA (Pradhan Mantri Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) parks for the textile industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In March 2023, the Government of India finalised the setting up of 7 PM MITRA (Pradhan Mantri Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) Parks across multiple states. (पीएम मित्र पार्क — 7 पार्क)

 

• The selected sites included locations in Tamil Nadu (Virudhunagar), Telangana (Warangal), Gujarat (Navsari), Karnataka (Kalaburagi), Madhya Pradesh (Dhar) and Uttar Pradesh (Lucknow), among others.

 

• The PM MITRA scheme, run by the Ministry of Textiles, aims to develop world-class, integrated textile parks offering an entire value chain — from spinning to garment manufacturing — at a single location under a 'plug and play' model.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The PM MITRA scheme was first announced in the Union Budget 2021-22, drawing inspiration from the 5F vision — Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign.

 

NOTE

 

• 9, 5, 2 (Options 1, 2, 3): These do not match the officially announced number of PM MITRA park sites, which was 7.

question: The Salal Project, also called the Salal Hydroelectric Power Station, is on which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chenab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Salal Project (Salal Hydroelectric Power Station) is located on the Chenab River in the Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir. (सलाल परियोजना — चिनाब नदी)

 

• It is operated by NHPC Limited (National Hydroelectric Power Corporation) and was one of the first major hydroelectric projects built on the Chenab.

 

• The project has an installed capacity distributed across two stages and has played an important role in power generation for the northern grid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important hydroelectric projects on the Chenab River include the Baglihar and Dulhasti projects, both also in Jammu and Kashmir.

 

NOTE

 

• Ganga (Option 1): Hosts projects like Tehri Dam (on a tributary), not the Salal Project.

 

• Ravi (Option 2): Hosts the Thein (Ranjit Sagar) Dam, not the Salal Project.

 

• Krishna (Option 3): Hosts projects like the Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar Dams, not the Salal Project.

question: When is National Javelin Day celebrated in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7th August.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Javelin Day is celebrated in India on 7 August every year, commemorating the day Neeraj Chopra won India's gold medal in Javelin Throw at the Tokyo Olympics (2020, held in 2021). (राष्ट्रीय भाला दिवस — 7 अगस्त)

 

• This was India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in athletics, and the day is observed to celebrate this historic achievement and promote the sport of javelin throw in India.

 

• Neeraj Chopra achieved this feat with a best throw of 87.58 metres in the final on 7 August 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 29 August is celebrated as National Sports Day in India, marking the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

 

NOTE

 

• 6th August, 12th January, 29th August (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these dates correspond to the date of Neeraj Chopra's Olympic javelin gold, which is commemorated as National Javelin Day.

question: In which of the following plants do roots arise from parts of a plant other than the radicle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monstera.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roots that arise from parts of a plant other than the radicle are called adventitious roots. (अपस्थानिक जड़ें — मॉन्स्टेरा)

 

• Monstera, a climbing plant, develops aerial adventitious roots that grow from its stem and branches rather than from the radicle; these roots help the plant climb, anchor itself, and absorb moisture and nutrients from the air.

 

• This is a classic textbook example (as in NCERT Science) of adventitious roots, alongside plants like the banyan tree.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roots that develop directly from the radicle of the seed are called the normal (tap) root system, seen in most dicot plants.

 

NOTE

 

• Turnip (Option 2): Has a taproot system — an enlarged taproot developing from the radicle, which is the edible part.

 

• Mustard plant (Option 3): Also has a typical taproot system arising from the radicle, with lateral roots branching off it.

 

• Maize (Option 4): Though maize does develop fibrous roots from the base of the stem, the standard textbook example used for roots arising from parts other than the radicle is Monstera, not maize.

question: What is Miyan ki Todi in Hindustani music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raag.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Miyan ki Todi is a Raag (Raga) in Hindustani classical music, believed to have been composed/popularised by the legendary court musician Miyan Tansen. (मियां की तोड़ी — राग)

 

• It belongs to the Todi thaat, one of the ten parent scales (thaats) of Hindustani music, and is traditionally performed in the late morning.

 

• Miyan ki Todi is known for its serious, contemplative mood and is one of the more revered ragas associated with the Tansen tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tansen, one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Emperor Akbar's court, is also credited with creating ragas like Miyan ki Malhar and Darbari Kanada.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhand (Option 1): Refers to metre/verse forms in Sanskrit and Hindi poetry, not a raga.

 

• Kirtan (Option 3): A form of devotional musical narration, typically involving call-and-response singing of hymns.

 

• Tanam (Option 4): A rhythmic, syllable-based improvisational element used in Carnatic music (as in Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi), not Hindustani music.

question: What is the literacy rate of males in India as per the report published in the National Survey of India-2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 84.7%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the report referenced (National Survey of India-2022), the male literacy rate in India was recorded at 84.7%. (भारत में पुरुष साक्षरता दर — 84.7%)

 

• Literacy rate figures are typically derived from large-scale national surveys that assess the proportion of the population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.

 

• Male literacy rates in India have historically been higher than female literacy rates, reflecting a persistent gender gap that successive government surveys and the Census have tracked over time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, the overall literacy rate of India was 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%; subsequent surveys have shown further improvement in these figures.

 

NOTE

 

• 83.4%, 86.3%, 81.2% (Options 1, 2, 4): These figures do not match the male literacy rate of 84.7% cited in the referenced 2022 survey report.
